How it works

Three steps between you and less repetition.

CommonCopy stays quietly in the Windows notification area or Mac menu bar until you need it.

1

Highlight or write

Save text you select in another app, or create a phrase directly in the manager.

2

Open CommonCopy

Use Ctrl + right-click on Windows or Command + right-click on Mac. A keyboard shortcut is available too.

3

Choose and continue

Choose a phrase and paste it into the field you were using. After saving captured text, the window closes so you can carry on.

Built for daily work

Simple enough to disappear. Useful enough to keep.

⌘

System-wide access

Open your phrases beside the cursor or with a keyboard shortcut while working in other applications.

＋

Capture highlighted text

Select text in a webpage, document, email, or PDF and save it as a categorized phrase from the same popup.

⌕

Fast search

Search phrase titles and text in the manager. Keep the quick menu small, with Favourites, Commonly Used, and nested categories.

★

Favourites and Commonly Used

Keep favourites close; sort commonly used phrases by use count, then most-recent use.

↕

Import and export

Move or back up your phrase library using a readable JSON file.

◎

Categories that fit you

Keep prompts under GPT, Image based, or a project name. Add subcategories and organize phrases in the way you work.

Privacy by design

Your phrases stay on your computer.

CommonCopy is local-first software. It does not need an account, an Internet connection, or a cloud service to do its job.

Read the privacy details

FAQ

Useful answers before you install.

Does CommonCopy work in every application?

It is designed for standard text fields on Windows and Mac. Some elevated, protected, remote, or unusually implemented applications may restrict copy and paste. Mac activation, capture, and paste require Accessibility permission.

Does it replace the normal right-click menu?

No. Your normal right-click remains unchanged. CommonCopy appears only when you use Ctrl + right-click on Windows, Command + right-click on Mac, or its keyboard shortcut.

Can it save text I highlight in another app?

Yes. Highlight selectable text, open CommonCopy, and choose Save highlighted text…. You can review the generated title and category before saving. Copy-protected or image-only content may not be available.

Where are my phrases stored?

CommonCopy stores them as local JSON under your user profile: AppData on Windows and Application Support on Mac. The manager provides import and export; the application also keeps a rotating previous-version backup.

Can I store passwords in CommonCopy?

No. The initial version stores phrases as readable local text. Use a dedicated password manager for passwords, authentication codes, and recovery keys.

Is CommonCopy open source?

The application uses the MIT license. Public source access and release information will be linked here when the project launches.

Will there be ads inside the app?

No. Advertising is limited to this website. No advertising provider is connected to this preview; the privacy page will explain the provider and any required choices before ads are enabled.

Your library. Your control.

CommonCopy’s desktop application is MIT licensed and stores phrases locally. Public release notes and source access will be available alongside the downloads.
